# AI Plugins

Convert files, compress media and PDFs, and edit PDFs from a compatible desktop AI agent using frogConvert. The existing MCP server does the work locally.

## Downloads

**Preview status:** The packages below are being validated in a draft pull request. They are not published releases yet. Preview ZIPs are generated by the [AI plugin packages workflow](https://github.com/ogfrench/frogConvert/actions/workflows/ai-plugins.yml) as build artifacts, not as public installers. After validation, versioned downloads and SHA-256 checksums will be available from [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/ogfrench/frogConvert/releases).

| Client | Package filename | Current status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Claude Code | `frogconvert-claude.zip` | Preview, requires Bun |
| ChatGPT Desktop | `frogconvert-chatgpt.zip` | Developer preview; local MCP access and distribution approval vary |

These are **not standalone binaries**. Both packages use the existing `bunx frogconvert@<version> mcp` command. They contain manifests, connection configuration, and four shared skills, not the conversion engine itself.

## Before installing

1. Install [Bun](https://bun.sh/) and ensure `bunx` is available in the PATH seen by the AI desktop client.
2. The machine must have network access on first invocation to fetch the pinned frogConvert npm package unless already cached.
3. Optional conversion engines (for example LibreOffice or FFmpeg) may be required for some formats. Browser-assisted conversions require a working local Chromium bridge and the engine assets. See [Integrations](INTEGRATIONS.md) for limitations.

## Claude Code

Extract `frogconvert-claude.zip` to a folder (for example `~/plugins/frogconvert`). Start Claude Code with the folder supplied to the plugin loader:

```sh
claude --plugin-dir /absolute/path/to/frogconvert
```

The ZIP includes a standard `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, `.mcp.json` and `skills/`. The agent should discover eight frogConvert MCP tools. The first initialization may take longer while fetching dependencies and compiling WebAssembly. This method is an initial local developer install; marketplace publishing is not yet configured.

Claude Cowork compatibility still needs a clean installation test. Do not assume Claude Code's `--plugin-dir` command works identically in Cowork.

## ChatGPT Desktop

The ChatGPT package has a portable Agent Plugins `plugin.json` and a local `stdio` MCP configuration. It requires a ChatGPT Desktop environment that supports **local MCP plugins**.

When your account or workspace exposes plugin ZIP upload, upload `frogconvert-chatgpt.zip` through the supported Plugins interface and verify that the local MCP server starts and all eight tools appear. Some workspace uploads require administrator permissions. Do not expect this integration to run from web or mobile chat.

**Distribution restriction:** OpenAI requires partner approval/allowlisting for public submissions of desktop-only plugins with local MCP servers. This developer-preview ZIP is not an approved public directory listing. See [desktop-only plugin requirements](https://developers.openai.com/plugins/deploy/desktop-only).

## What you can ask

- "Convert these TIFF images into PNG files without changing the originals."
- "Compress these PDFs without changing their format."
- "Merge these three PDFs in the order given."
- "Extract pages 2 through 5 into a new PDF."
- "Which conversions can frogConvert perform in this environment?"

The packages include `convert-files`, `compress-files`, `edit-pdfs` and `inspect-formats` skills. Their tools are the same eight tools documented in [MCP Integrations](INTEGRATIONS.md).

## Privacy and filesystem permissions

frogConvert's local MCP execution reads input file paths and writes output paths on your machine. It does not use a hosted conversion backend, but **the AI client may process filenames, paths, file contents, prompts or tool results** according to that provider's policies. Avoid embedding large files as base64 in prompts.

The MCP server can write to arbitrary paths unless `FROGCONVERT_SANDBOX_ROOT` is set. Its current lexical containment check is **not a secure filesystem sandbox against symlinks**. Review the tool calls and outputs before approving them. The browser bridge currently uses Chromium with `--no-sandbox`; avoid processing untrusted documents with it until this is hardened. Keep originals.

See [Security](../SECURITY.md) and [the integration reference](INTEGRATIONS.md) for the full security model.

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | What to check |
| --- | --- |
| No tools appear | Desktop/local MCP support, plugin enabled, restart the client |
| `bunx` not found | Bun installation and desktop client's PATH |
| Package startup fails | Check the pinned npm version is published; ensure initial network access |
| Conversion route missing | Inspect `list_formats` and optional native dependencies |
| Browser-assisted conversion fails | Chromium, production `dist/` assets, bridge setup |
| File access denied | Client permissions and `FROGCONVERT_SANDBOX_ROOT` |

These preview packages intentionally have no installation hooks, no account requirement, and no automatic privilege escalation.
